regressions.source: L2ERC20ExtendedTokensBridge.sol:96, 112 emit WithdrawalInitiated(_getL1Token(l2Token_), l2Token_, msg.sender, to_, amount_, data_)
regressions.issue: The event's bytes argument was decoded as Array(len=_param4.length, data=_param4[all]) and is now its raw ABI encoding: the offset 96 plus a memory slice holding the length, the data and the padding. The buffer is now addressed past the reused sendMessage buffer (mem[64] + ceil32(len) + 260 ...) and is no longer recognised. Still exact.
regressions.rule: Recognise the ABI encoding of a bytes argument wherever its buffer lies: an offset word k followed, at head + k, by a length word L, L data bytes copied from a calldata parameter and zero padding to ceil32(L) is Array(len=L, data=param[all]). The base may be any symbolic pointer.

improvements: The sendMessage call's bytes message no longer goes through a copy loop (whiles 15 -> 13). It prints as Array(len=ceil32(len) + 228, data=...) with its content visible on the line before (selector 0xa9f9e675, l1Token 0, l2Token, from, to, amount, offset 192, data); the padding length was checked. Dead bridgeBurn buffer writes are gone. The storage slot 0x013e92... shows whole bytes in def storage and the 4 mapping-key writes.
notes: Diff of 182 lines, read in full (6 functions; 4 only by hex display). Calls, events, storage writes and reverts are unchanged in count; only the copy loop went. The new text prints part of the sendMessage buffer before the call (selector, target 0, length, gas limit) but not the offset 96: dead or redundant writes beside a decoded call (P8).
summary: One medium regression: WithdrawalInitiated's bytes argument, decoded before, is now a raw memory slice in withdraw and withdrawTo. The sendMessage call's message is better (no copy loop, content visible).
